title: 材料科学Ⅱ
subtitle: Materials Science II
keywords: Iron and steel materials 2.Non-ferrous materials 3.Equilibrium phase diagram 4.Microstructure control 5.Phase transformation
educationalGoal: To design and manufacture machines and structures that exhibit superior performance, it is necessary to select materials based on an understanding of the characteristics of the elements of which they are composed. In addition, the microstructures and properties of materials change after heat treatment and processing. In this course, students learn how to modify materials by heat treatment and processing.
advice: The outline of the class is as follows: Fe-C phase diagram and normal microstructures Heat treatment and microstructure of steel Work hardening, recovery, and re-crystallization Solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening, and crystal grain refinement strengthening
requiredKnowledge: It is strongly recommended that students take this course after reviewing and fully understanding the contents of Materials Science I.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the relationship between an Fe-C phase diagram and normal microstructures.
Be able to explain basic heat-treatment methods for steel.
Be able to explain basic heat-treatment methods for aluminum alloys.
Be able to explain microstructures obtained by plastic deformation, and recovery and re-crystallization

achievementLevels.ideal: 1: Explain the formation process of normal microstructures in carbon steels using an Fe-C phase diagram. 2: Propose heat-treatment conditions of steels using the Fe-C phase diagram, continuous cooling transformation (CCT) curve, and time-temperature transformation (TTT) curve. 2 and 3: Explain the relationship between mechanical properties and phase transformation and/or precipitation caused by heat treatment. 4: Explain the recovery and re-crystallization process for work-hardened materials.
achievementLevels.standard: 1: Explain the relation between carbon content in carbon steels and normal microstructures. 2 and 3: Explain basic technical terms of heat treatment, for example, quenching, tempering, annealing, normalizing, solid-solution treatment, and aging. 4: Explain the relationship between work-hardening and lattice defects.

lessons.content: Lecture: Course introduction Self-check: Review incomplete knowledge from Materials Science I. Develop future learning plans.
lessons.assignments: Understand the course objectives. Review Materials Science I.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn the characteristic points (e.g., melting point, transformation point, eutectic point, and eutectoid point) expressed as an Fe-C phase diagram and the formation process of a normal microstructure.
lessons.assignments: Review how to use a phase diagram.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn the basics of heat treatment for carbon steel and phase transformation of carbon steel.
lessons.assignments: Review crystal structures of alpha, gamma, and delta phases in Fe-C phase diagram

lessons.content: Quiz 1: Check your level of understanding of classes 1-3. Lecture: Understand the relationship between mechanical properties and microstructure obtained by heat treatment.
lessons.assignments: Review the content of classes 1-3 to prepare for Quiz 1.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review Quiz 1 and its answers. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Lecture: Learn the TTT curve (also called the S curve) and CCT curve.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 1-4 to answer your questions.

lessons.content: Lecture: Further learn the TTT curve and CCT curve.
lessons.assignments: Review technical terms of heat treatment using JIS G0201.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn tempering and temper brittleness of steels. Learn the Charpy pendulum impact test to evaluate temper brittleness.
lessons.assignments: Study JIS Z2242, “Method for Charpy pendulum impact test of metallic materials.”

lessons.content: Quiz 2: Check the level of understanding of lectures from classes 4-7. Lecture: Understand the outline of microstructure control and material strengthening.

Self-reflection class: Review Quiz 2 and its answer. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Lecture: Learn microstructure control with plastic working and heat treatment. Understand the mechanisms of microstructure control with work hardening, recovery, and re-crystallization.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 1-8. Review technical terms of microstructure control.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn solid solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening. Understand characteristics of aluminum alloys subjected to these strengthening techniques.
lessons.assignments: Research relation between strengthening mechanisms and dislocations after the class.
Research relation between strengthening mechanisms and crystal grain refinement after the class.

lessons.content: Quiz 3: Check your level of understanding of lectures from classes 8-12. Integrated learning: Discuss the functions of materials in mechanical engineering.

Self-reflection class: Review the answers of Quiz 3. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Integrated learning: To deepen your understanding of this course, a Q&A session is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Review your notes, the textbook, and other materials before the class.

lessons.content: Integrated learning: Review the content of all classes. Exam: Evaluate the degree of your achievement for the entire course.
lessons.assignments: Review the content of all classes.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review the exam and its answers. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Self-check: Self-check of the quiz, exam, and report. Consider the future learning plan.
lessons.operation: Review the exam Study exam answers and request explanations as needed Review comments on the graded report
